title: Enlighten, Autopilot, and summaries
blurb: Autopilot (Omilia), voice versus chat, AutoSummary types, and Copilot on a foreign ACD.

lessons.title: Autopilot is Autopilot (Omilia)
lessons.summary: Autopilot (Omilia) is a virtual agent for voice and digital. It uses Experience Optimization data plus your interaction data. The Classics, Inc. story on the page is NiCE's example.
objectives: Separate voice from text at the start
Treat Edward Ferrars as the doc example

p: NiCE CXone Autopilot (Omilia) handles voice and digital interactions in place of live agents. It uses CXone Experience Optimization data, described as over 30 years of interaction data, plus your organization's data, to build flows of utterances and responses.
The page's story about Edward Ferrars and Classics, Inc. is NiCE's example of switching intents. It is not a customer case study you can cite as a deployment.

lessons.title: Voice and text do not connect the same way
lessons.summary: Voice uses a SIP backchannel and stays connected until complete or transfer. Text uses Virtual Agent Hub and the script on each turn. Voice setup needs NiCE. Text needs Digital Experience.
objectives: Send voice setup to the account representative

p: A voice contact calls a number and may hit an IVR first. Utterances are transcribed. CXone stays connected to the virtual agent service and does not participate in the conversation. It waits for complete or transfer. The page calls this the SIP backchannel method.
Setting up Autopilot for voice requires assistance from NiCE. Contact the account representative. Recording of those voice interactions uses Recording Management.
Text starts in a chat window. Utterances are already text. Requests and responses go through Virtual Agent Hub and the script on each turn, which allows turn-by-turn customization.
Text virtual agents require Digital Experience and work with chat-based digital channels. At the end, the virtual agent signals the script to end or to request a live agent.

lessons.title: The four pieces of an Autopilot integration
lessons.summary: You need a configured channel, Virtual Agent Hub, a Studio script with a virtual agent action on the point of contact, and a configured Autopilot virtual agent.
objectives: Put the action on the POC script
Keep Knowledge and Voice Biometrics as named relatives

p: The page requires NiCE CXone with a voice or digital chat channel, Virtual Agent Hub for provider connection and transcription options, at least one Studio script whose virtual agent action is on the point of contact's script, and a fully configured Autopilot (Omilia) virtual agent.
Transcription and speech synthesis can happen in CXone or, in some cases, on the provider platform.

Key facts say Autopilot (Omilia) is different from Autopilot Knowledge and from Voice Biometrics. The same page also says you can use voice biometrics with an Autopilot voice virtual agent, including the Omilia miniapp.
Both sentences stay. A different product can still be attached. This lesson does not copy enrollment clicks.

lessons.title: TTS voices and a knowledge base
lessons.summary: Standard TTS voices are in the subscription. Premium voices are bring-your-own. A knowledge base needs Knowledge Hub. This lesson does not invent prices.

p: Standard voices for Autopilot (Omilia) on the page include Omilia native, Google Standard, WaveNet, and Neural2, Microsoft Neural, and AWS Standard and Neural. Amelia's standard list on the page is Google Standard, WaveNet, Neural2, and Polyglot.

Premium voices such as ElevenLabs, Google Chirp3, and others require a direct agreement with the provider. The page says Autopilot still uses per-session pricing. It does not publish a price, and neither does this lab.

You can connect NiCE CXone Knowledge Management (Expert) or a third-party knowledge base. Using those sources requires Knowledge Hub. The bot can answer from articles, include links and images, or link the full article.
If the contact does not find it helpful, the interaction is forwarded to a live agent. How the knowledge is used is a conversational-flow setting.

lessons.title: Three AutoSummary types
lessons.summary: AutoSummary writes a summary after voice or digital messaging. Types are Structured AI, Generative AI, and Hybrid. Email is not supported. Agents can edit.
objectives: Quote the timing the page gives

p: Structured AI uses short phrases for intent, outcomes, and events. Generative AI is prose from the LLM. Hybrid sends Structured AI sentences to the generative service and returns complete sentences.
The page's examples are about a payment. They are examples of shape, not a script you must copy.

It works on voice and digital messaging. It does not currently support email. Summaries typically appear in 5 to 10 seconds. A spinner in the Notes field may last up to 60 seconds, which the page calls expected. After that, the request timed out and the agent can type notes.
Length can be configured between 40 and 250 words. Agents can modify the text and must save it.

choices: Structured AI, Generative AI, and Hybrid

lessons.title: What setup actually requires
lessons.summary: An account representative enables AutoSummary and Agent Assist Hub. You then need a profile, Studio, skills with disposition, and a transcription profile. MAX also needs a Copilot for Agents license.

p: You work with the account representative for the initial enablement. Agent Assist Hub must be enabled. Then you create at least one profile, create or modify Studio scripts, and create or modify skills that have the Disposition option for post-contact work.
You also create one or more transcription profiles for Continuous Stream Transcription. Voice audio is transcribed before the model runs.
AutoSummary works with Agent Workspace, the browser extension (Agent Integrated), embedded, Teams, Salesforce Agent, and MAX.

To use it with MAX instead of an agent application, you also need a Copilot for Agents license and Copilot for Agents set up. The summary for MAX is a pop-up the agent can copy into disposition notes.

lessons.title: Where the summary goes after the agent
lessons.summary: Other agents see the summary only if it is mapped to a CRM. The Contact mapping uses Disposition Notes. A Final Summary API can return the AI text or the edited text for two days. Cisco and Avaya can use it through Engagement Hub when Copilot is enabled.
objectives: Keep Engagement Hub Copilot as a separate gate

p: Without a CRM integration, other agents do not see the generated summaries. Mapping is on the Agent Integrations page: Contact entity type, NiCE CXone data field Disposition Notes, aimed at the CRM field you want.
Interaction Analytics can also filter on the intents, actions, and outcomes in the summaries.

The Final Summary API returns the AI summary by default. Add editedSummary=true for the agent-edited version, and only if the agent saved an edit before disposition. Data is available for two days. After that the API returns a generic no-response message rather than the original summary. Endpoint details stay on the developer portal.

On select Cisco and Avaya ACDs, AutoSummary is available when calls are recorded through Engagement Hub and Multi-ACD Engagement Hub is enabled for Copilot. Legacy AutoSummary, self-service, customer journey, legacy RTIG, and Actions are not supported on that path.
